questions.prompt: How do you think Peggy was feeling toward Shaun at that moment? Why do you say that?
questions.passage: The intensity of the sunlight was distressing. The shiny metal table reflected the light glaringly and Peggy, realising that she had left her sunglasses at home, could feel a headache coming on. If Shaun had been ready on time, they could have had a table under the trees, or one with an umbrella. He came back from placing their order, and took the chair opposite Peggy who folded her arms and pressed her lips together tightly.
questions.markingGuide: The student must identify Peggy's emotion (angry/annoyed/frustrated/irritated at Shaun) AND provide evidence. Accept: 'angry/annoyed because Shaun wasn't ready on time so they missed a shady table, and she folded her arms and pressed her lips tightly', 'frustrated because if Shaun had been on time they would have shade, and her body language shows she's upset (folded arms, pressed lips)', 'cross with Shaun because his lateness caused them to get the bad table in the sun and now she has a headache'. Must include BOTH the emotion AND at least one piece of evidence (body language OR the lateness causing the sun problem). Reject 'sad' or 'happy' — the body language (folded arms, pressed lips) clearly indicates anger/annoyance, not sadness.
